channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Korea’s Lee Faces Pushback as Trump Ups Pressure Over Hormuz
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung’s approval rating fell to a new low amid growing opposition over potential deployment of troops to the Strait of Hormuz, highlighting the political risks for the South Korean leader as he weighs options after US pressure to help secure the strategic waterway.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Katayama Calls Bessent’s ‘House’ Remark Scary in Translation
item.description: Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s recent reference to himself as “the house” sounded a little frightening when translated into Japanese, while saying she understood the expression reflected the secretary’s former role as a hedge-fund manager.
item.dc:creator: Erica Yokoyama

item.title: Vance Asks Voters To Stick With GOP, Nods To Iran War Angst
item.description: Vice President JD Vance urged voters to stick with the Republican party even if they disagree with the Trump administration on some issues — a call to look beyond tensions with the MAGA movement and frustration over the war in Iran.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove

item.title: Putin Lands in India for BRICS Summit Shaped by Wars, Tariffs
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in India for a BRICS summit with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and other leaders, as wars in the Middle East and Ukraine test the bloc’s push for greater economic clout and a bigger voice in global affairs.
item.dc:creator: Swati Pandey

item.title: Trump Says He Would Be GOP’s ‘Blocker’ If Democrats Win Midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump said he would serve as a “blocker” if Republicans lose control of Congress in November’s midterm elections, undercutting his warning that Democrats would pose a dangerous threat to American life should they win.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian

item.title: RNC Day 2 Underway in Dallas
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, US Interior Secretary Doug Burgum says Congress should approve President Donald Trump's $5,000 payment for Americans. Texas Attorney General and Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton discusses his tight race against Democrat James Talarico. Rep. Rick Crawford (R-AR), Chair of the House Intelligence Committee, says Iran’s ability to continue producing ballistic missiles remains part of the threat posed by its nuclear ambitions. Rep. Jason Crow (D-CO) says Congress has the constitutional authority to end the war with Iran, arguing the conflict is costing hundreds of billions of dollars and contributing to higher energy prices. US Housing and Urban Development Secretary Scott Turner discusses the efforts to lower housing and mortgage costs amid rising bond yields and borrowing rates. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s Housing Chief Stresses Cutting Rules as Aiding Buyers
item.description: The Trump administration is trying to help Americans better afford homes by cutting regulation, Housing and Urban Development Secretary Scott Turner said Thursday on Bloomberg Television.
item.dc:creator: Katy O'Donnell

item.title: Rep. Crow Thinks Congress Should and Can End Iran War
item.description: Rep. Jason Crow (D-CO) says Congress has the constitutional authority to end the war with Iran, arguing the conflict is costing hundreds of billions of dollars and contributing to higher energy prices. Rep. Crow says the US cannot permanently prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon through military action alone and calls for a permanent, verifiable diplomatic agreement. Rep. Crow says Democrats should reinstate ACA subsidies to bring health-care premiums under control and argues that Congress urgently needs a nonpartisan approach to AI regulation and guardrails. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Crawford: Iran Ballistic Missiles Remain Nuclear Threat
item.description: Rep. Rick Crawford (R-AR), Chair of the House Intelligence Committee, says Iran’s ability to continue producing ballistic missiles remains part of the threat posed by its nuclear ambitions and says he would like to see the conflict resolved sooner rather than later. Rep. Crawford says he wants oil below $80 a barrel and raises questions about whether Iran may be circumventing sanctions through in-kind support from China. Rep. Crawford says he likes the idea of President Trump’s proposed dividend checks but that any spending decision should be considered in light of the national debt. The show previews the interview ahead of the full conversation tomorrow on geopolitics and the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: HUD Secretary Turner on Bringing Down Housing Costs
item.description: US Housing and Urban Development Secretary Scott Turner discusses the efforts to lower housing and mortgage costs amid rising bond yields and borrowing rates. He outlines the administration’s strategy of deregulation. He speaks on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why India Won’t Break Up With Russia
item.description: India has spent decades balancing ties to Russia, and the USSR before it, with those to the US. Even now, amid the Kremlin’s war on Ukraine and intense pressure from Washington, New Delhi won’t let Moscow go. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Burgum Says Congress Role in Trump’s $5,000 Payment Plan Unclear
item.description: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said it’s unclear whether congressional approval would be needed to fulfill President Donald Trump’s pledge to provide $5,000 dividend payments to Americans if Republicans sweep the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Ari Natter and Kailey Leinz

item.title: Oracle Earnings Beat as Cloud Revenue Surges
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Duke University Professor of Finance Cam Harvey, Morningstar Senior Equity Analyst David Swartz, Philip Morris International Group CEO Jacek Olczak, Citi Wealth Head of Portfolio Advisory Jeanne Sun, RBC Capital Markets Software Equity Research Managing Director Rishi Jaluria, Janus Henderson Global Head, Client Portfolio Management Seth Meyer, SMAC Entertainment CEO & Co-Founder Constance Schwartz-Morini, DraftKings CEO Jason Robins, & Fanatics Betting & Gaming CEO Matt King. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Loyalist Tapped to Lead Controversial DOJ Probe Quits
item.description: Joseph diGenova, a loyal ally of President Donald Trump chosen to lead a sprawling criminal investigation into whether former government officials conspired to stymie him, has resigned.
item.dc:creator: Chris Strohm and Jimmy Jenkins

item.title: Texas AG Paxton on Senate Race, Trump Dividend and AI
item.description: Texas Attorney General and Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton discusses his tight race against Democrat James Talarico and the impact of President Donald Trump’s support, including a reported $10 million contribution and roughly $27 million in total ad spending. Speaking on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition," Paxton also comments on the backlash against AI data centers and the war in Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Brazil Election: Bolsonaro Surges in Poll as Supreme Court Crisis Weighs on Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro surged into a tie with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in a new poll, erasing a 4.5-point gap as a crisis inside Brazil’s Supreme Court weighs on the leftist leader’s reelection bid.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Diniz Tavares

item.title: JD Vance’s Republican Midterm Convention Speech to Spotlight 2028 Race
item.description: Donald Trump headed to Dallas looking for a rebound in Republican fortunes. JD Vance’s future likely hinges on it.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove

item.title: Trump $5,000 Check Plan Gets Cool Reception From GOP Allies
item.description: President Donald Trump’s proposal to send $5,000 checks to every adult US citizen if Republicans sweep the November midterms prompted a lukewarm response from members of his party in Congress, which controls federal spending.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis, María Paula Mijares Torres, Caitlin Reilly and Erik Wasson

item.title: Trump Promises $500 Back for Obamacare Plans Republicans Cut
item.description: The Trump administration pledged to send $500 each to nearly 1 million Americans it said paid too much for federally backed Obamacare health insurance, whose funding was at the center of a political standoff that led to last year’s record-long government shutdown.
item.dc:creator: Ike Swetlitz and Melos Ambaye

item.title: Xi’s First India Trip Since 2019 Offers Olive Branch to Modi
item.description: When Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in New Delhi this weekend for his first post-Covid visit to India, he faces the task of managing a delicate detente with his neighbor and rival.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
